Papa Zaka's Harvest Fruit Medley

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 6-8Prep 25 min

This vibrant Tropical Fruit Medley is a perfect offering and celebratory dish for Fete de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa in Haitian Vodou. Papa Zaka, the spirit of agriculture and harvest, is honored with the bounty of the land, and this fresh, colorful assortment of fruits symbolizes the richness and sweetness of a successful harvest. It's a simple yet profound way to connect with the earth's generosity.

Ingredients

  • 1 large ripe mango (about 1.5 lbs / 680g)
  • 1 medium ripe papaya (about 1 lb / 450g)
  • 1/2 fresh pineapple (about 1.5 lbs / 680g before peeling)
  • 2 ripe bananas
  • 1 star fruit (carambola)
  • Juice of 1 lime (about 2 tablespoons / 30ml)
  • Optional: 1 tablespoon (15ml) honey or maple syrup
  • Optional: Fresh mint leaves for garnish

Method

  1. Thoroughly wash all fruits under cool running water.
  2. Carefully peel the mango, papaya, and pineapple. Dice them into uniform, bite-sized pieces and place them in a large mixing bowl.
  3. Just before serving, peel the bananas and slice them into rounds. Add them to the bowl with the other fruits.
  4. Slice the star fruit crosswise into star-shaped pieces and add them to the fruit mixture.
  5. Gently toss all the fruits together in the bowl.
  6. Drizzle the fresh lime juice over the fruit. If desired, add the honey or maple syrup and gently toss again to coat evenly.
  7. Transfer the fruit medley to a serving platter or individual bowls. Garnish with fresh mint leaves, if using, before presenting.

Tips

  • For the best flavor, ensure all fruits are perfectly ripe but still firm enough to hold their shape when cut.
  • Feel free to customize the medley with other tropical fruits like kiwi, passion fruit, or lychees, depending on availability.
  • A sprinkle of shredded coconut or a tiny pinch of freshly grated ginger can add an extra layer of tropical flavor.
